content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or bullish sentiment (especially when sentiment > 0.00); model tends to overreact and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged bearish sentiment or low sentiment windows (sentiment = 0.00 or near-zero); model often misses downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods (e.g., 1st few days of 30d horizon) — adjust for immediate volatility or news-driven shifts.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are rising, model often overshoots peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment > 0.20.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For low sentiment periods, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment < 0.10.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply “reversal penalty” by reducing forecast 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops below 0.00.
